triggers: claims about embodied or physical-world AI safety, deployment, hazards, failures, assurance, or residual risk
evidence_standards: Define the system boundary, operational domain, exposed people and assets, and relevant lifecycle phase.
Trace every safety claim to hazards, failure modes, controls, verification evidence, and residual uncertainty.
Distinguish observed safety evidence from assumptions, simulations, proxies, and proposed safeguards.
Test foreseeable misuse, distribution shift, degraded operation, human interaction, and control handoff where relevant.
State the population, environment, duration, and conditions beyond which evidence does not generalize.
safety_constraints: Do not equate absence of observed harm with demonstrated safety.
Do not describe a system as safe without an explicit claim scope, evidence chain, and residual-risk statement.
Do not recommend real-world exposure when the evidence supports only a laboratory, simulation, or conceptual claim.
